clue.text: Fish seen round right channel

indicators.note: round means the fish's name is placed around the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Someone spots a fish circling in a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch, so a channel cut in the ground.

clue.text: John Cleese is unbelievable

definitions.meaning: the comic actor is famously lanky, about six foot five
a far-fetched story is a ... story or ... tale

explanation.definitionFit: Cleese is a very lofty man, and a tall tale is one that strains belief.

clue.text: Unsure comments about quisling a mistake

indicators.note: about means the hesitation noises stand on either side of the traitor

parts.note: er and um are the noises of someone hesitating, the two unsure remarks
the second of the two hesitating noises
a quisling is a traitor, and a rat is slang for one who betrays

explanation.surface: Someone hums and hahs over a traitor's error.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in print, so a mistake listed for correction.

clue.text: Go away following smack round side of head

indicators.note: round means the blow word goes around the body part

parts.note: a clout is a heavy blow or smack
an ear sits on either side of the head

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave after being hit about the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' is a link word joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear out is to leave a place, an idiom for going away.

clue.text: Cold store one touches shivering, temperature nowhere at end of Yule

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: shivering suggests trembling movement, so the remaining letters are jumbled
nowhere says the temperature letter is to be found nowhere in the word touches, so it is dropped
end of picks the last letter of Yule

explanation.surface: A shivering person at Christmas touches something cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nowhere' drops T from TOUCHES, leaving OUCHES, which 'shivering' rearranges to CEHOUS; E is the end of Yule.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice house was a building for storing ice, a cold store before refrigeration.

clue.text: Short ball dismissing opener, South American caught at close of play

parts.note: curt means short or brusque

indicators.note: caught means the remaining letters hold the people's name inside them
dismissing opener means the first letter of the ball word is sent off

parts.note: a ball as a dance or as a thing thrown
the Inca were a people of the Andes in South America

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a short ball removes the opening batsman, a South American caught at stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface misleads: 'dismissing opener' drops B from BALL, leaving ALL, which holds INCA.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain call is the final bow at the end of a theatre performance, the close of a play.

clue.text: Artist misses his fifth game

indicators.note: misses his fifth means the artist's name loses its fifth letter

parts.note: David Hockney is a celebrated British painter

explanation.surface: A painter fails to make a fifth attempt at a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Hockey is a team sport played with sticks and a ball, a game.

clue.text: Loosened shoe — and clue too?

indicators.note: too says the clue words are loosened as well, as the shoe is, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shoe has come loose, and so, apparently, has the clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoe' completes the surface picture; 'too' means the words 'and clue' are loosened like the shoe, giving the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Laces untied leave a shoe slack, so unlaced means loosened.

clue.text: Medium substance, though maximum in camels, perhaps

indicators.note: in means the maximum word goes inside the rearranged letters
perhaps hints the word camels may be in some other order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: top means maximum, as in top speed

explanation.surface: A strange substance is found inside camels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the camels letters as ECLASM, and 'in' sets the maximum word inside after EC. 'though' only joins; 'Medium' means a spiritualist, not a size.
explanation.definitionFit: Ectoplasm is the substance spiritualist mediums claimed to exude in seances.

clue.text: Sound of car in store

indicators.note: sound of says the car's name is to be heard, giving a word that sounds like it in a non-rhotic accent

parts.note: the Lada is a Russian make of car

explanation.surface: The noise of a car in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: In a southern British accent, with no R sound, the car name and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool room or cupboard for storing food.

clue.text: Couple to hire band

parts.note: a brace is a pair or couple, as of game birds
to let is to hire out a property

explanation.surface: Two people set out to engage a group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is a band worn around the wrist.

clue.text: Exaggerated trouble brewing?

parts.note: read one way, a big fuss over little; read another, turbulent weather inside a vessel where tea is brewing

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a great fuss over a trivial matter, an overblown upset.

clue.text: Titanic is labouring

definitions.meaning: the liner sank and lies on the floor of the Atlantic, far below the surface
labouring means struggling or in serious difficulty

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in serious trouble, while the sunken liner literally rests in the ocean depths.

clue.text: Excuse me and you breaking in, having broken apart

clue.text: Petit déjeuner, one tucked away by worker in a bad mood?

indicators.note: tucked away means the numeral is put inside the mood word

parts.note: cross means annoyed or in a bad mood
I is the Roman numeral for one
the worker ant is the crosswords' standard worker

explanation.surface: A grumpy worker hides something at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word; the bad-mood word comes first in the answer although the worker is named first.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is the crescent pastry typical of a French breakfast, which is what petit déjeuner means.

clue.text: Clue short of perfect

indicators.note: short of means the perfect word is cut back by its last letter

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A hint that falls just below perfection.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no idea means having no clue, so the two are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Chinese daughter upset, featuring in "The Revolutionary Playboy"

indicators.note: featuring in means the turned letters appear inside the other word
revolutionary suggests turning round, so the first letter of the word is moved to the end

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: Sino- is the prefix meaning Chinese
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A Chinese woman is distressed to appear in a film about a revolutionary womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' rotates the first word so its T goes to the end, giving HET; 'upset' gives DONIS, which sits inside it. The quoted title is pure surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedonist lives for pleasure, as a playboy does.

clue.text: Perverted fun going in for gynaecology

indicators.note: going in says the answer lies inside the next words of the clue

explanation.surface: Some twisted amusement is had in a gynaecology clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild bout of debauchery, depraved fun.

clue.text: One following star in the sky in foreign region, endlessly

indicators.note: in means the sky word goes inside the rearranged letters
foreign suggests something strange, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly means the word region loses its last letter

parts.note: up means aloft or in the sky

explanation.surface: Someone tracks a star across a foreign sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves REGIO, which 'foreign' rearranges as GROIE; the first 'in' belongs to the sky phrase, the second is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A groupie is a devoted fan who follows a pop star around.

clue.text: Terrible fears about salary for many, where work stinks

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters are placed around the pay word
terrible suggests something mangled, so the letters of fears are rearranged

parts.note: a wage is pay or salary
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: Someone dreads low pay in a job that is unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' gives SEFAR, split around the pay word; 'for' only joins. M for many comes from the Roman thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewage farm is a place where waste is treated, so the work there literally smells.

clue.text: Wonderful air, thinner

parts.note: ace means excellent or wonderful
an air is a tune, and tone is sound or tune

explanation.surface: A lovely melody that is more slender.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a solvent used as a paint thinner and nail-varnish remover.

clue.text: Prepared for issue, seeing world of computers indeed incomprehensible

indicators.note: in, taken from the word indeed, means the computing letters go inside
incomprehensible suggests garbled, so the letters of deed are rearranged

parts.note: IT, information technology, is the world of computers

explanation.surface: Computing jargon is truly baffling to someone preparing a publication.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'indeed' splits as 'in' (container signal) and 'deed' (anagram fodder, giving EDED around IT); 'seeing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Text that is edited has been readied for publication, prepared for issue.

clue.text: One taking down points as broadcaster holds script in front of panel

indicators.note: holds means the broadcaster word contains the others

parts.note: a sower broadcasts seed by scattering it

indicators.note: in front of means the script word comes before the panel word

parts.note: the words of a play are its script
a wall panel is a section of wall

explanation.surface: A radio presenter keeps a script before an interview panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcaster' suggests radio but means one who scatters seed. 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword swallower takes sharp-pointed blades down the throat.

clue.text: Port removed from bottle?

definitions.meaning: A port city in the south of Ireland
a bottle stopper made from bark is pulled out before pouring

explanation.definitionFit: The Irish harbour city shares its name with the stopper drawn from a wine bottle.

clue.text: A party leader amid change to remove member

indicators.note: amid means the party's first letter goes inside the change word

parts.note: to mutate is to change

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of party

explanation.surface: A party leader in the middle of a reshuffle wants to get rid of a member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' looks political but means a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To amputate is to cut off a limb, and member is an old word for limb.

clue.text: Roosevelt's logical statement not entirely grabbing party

indicators.note: grabbing means the shortened word holds the party word
not entirely means the statement word loses its last letter

parts.note: a theorem is a statement proved by logic
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A US president's argument is not quite complete and seizes the party.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the president's first name: Theodore Roosevelt was the 26th US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore was the forename of the US president Teddy Roosevelt.

clue.text: Take off, with all taken off

definitions.text: Take off, with all taken off

parts.words: Take off, with all taken off
parts.note: to dash off quickly while wearing no clothes at all

explanation.definitionFit: Streaking is running naked through a public place, often a sports ground.
